changes.details: Added dependency_lock with an explicit 8 MiB byte limit. The binary stream reads no more than cap + 1 before rejecting overflow, and only accepted bounded bytes are decoded as strict UTF-8. CRLF/CR normalization preserves the prior text contract.

Root preparation compares pathname metadata before/after and opened-descriptor metadata before/after, verifies selected/opened device and inode, and requires the returned byte count to equal the stable opened size. Same-size edits, growth and replacement reject. Each stat API is compared with itself because Windows stat/fstat ctime values differ.

Added eight focused test methods covering cap - 1 and exact-cap UTF-8 acceptance, cap + 1 before decode, growth after fstat, malformed UTF-8, CRLF/CR, same-size mutation, separate before-open and after-read replacement cases, and descriptor closure on read failure.

tests.details: First implementation compared complete Path.stat metadata directly with os.fstat metadata. Windows ctime semantics caused normal, UTF-8 and newline cases to reject as integrity errors. These are subtest entries, not seven distinct failed test methods.
After metadata comparison was changed to path-to-path and descriptor-to-descriptor with device/inode identity linkage.
Existing dependency/workspace security settings, exact overrides, real current lock, source packaging and related unit-boundary assertions remain passing.
Final tests after parent review split the simulated pathname substitution into explicit before-open and after-read subcases, with lookup-count assertions. No production code changed after sequence 2.

otherChecks.details: Both modified/new Python files parsed with ast.parse. UTF-8, LF termination and absence of trailing whitespace checked. Final edited test file was also executed by sequence 4.

fixStageObservations.details: Initial strict metadata cross-comparison was not portable because Windows stat and fstat reported different ctime values for the same unchanged file. No checks were dropped: each API now has its own before/after comparison and both identities must agree.

Parent review found the first pathname-replacement fixture intercepted the initial lookup as well as the final one, so its comment overstated after-read race coverage. Final tests exercise both specific lookup positions separately.

limitations: Only the eight new test methods and six existing BoundaryTests methods were run. Repeated runs cover corrections to the same tests and are not additional unique coverage.

Tests ran on Windows Python 3.12.14. The pathname replacement cases substitute individual stat results instead of relying on Linux unlink-of-open-file behavior. Same-size mutation and file growth use actual isolated temporary files.
No Linux/SSH/systemd probe, full suite, network provider, personal configuration or online instance was accessed. This repair does not claim a new clean audit round or deployment acceptance.

No existing tests, documentation, feature evidence or audit ledger were changed. Source and test changes require the parent to refresh relevant current-source coverage pointers and restart the clean-audit gate.
